guide.title: Test an idea for {{name}}.
guide.body:
• Explore the real bus, tram and rail patterns. Click a line in the list or on the map.
  • Reduce map clutter with the mode buttons in the bottom-bar Layers menu. They hide routes, stops and vehicles without changing the network.
  • Tinker with its service interval, active state and stops. The stats compare your scenario with the baseline.
  • Build a metro from map clicks, optionally close it into a one-direction ring, or load a documented past concept as an editable draft.
  • Plan with resident density or tram-and-rail access layers. The left rail collapses the single desktop panel, which expands on hover or click. Network, Inspect and Results share it; mobile tabs open the same views.
  • Play the illustrative vehicle animation. Use Undo, Reset, Export and Import to manage scenarios.
guide.map: Map: drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom. Right-click for location data, line actions and the ruler. While drawing, right-click a station to move or remove it, or middle-drag it. Click a stop to see its service intervals. Press F for fullscreen; Display settings can hide its button. Right-drag on empty map space to rotate.

data.title: Real network. Estimated outcomes.
data.area: The playable area covers {{count}} municipalities in {{name}}. Outlying endpoints provide transit context.
data.population: The mask uses published 1 km polygons, including zero-resident cells. Cells are selected by their centers inside {{count}} municipal boundaries, so totals are not exact full-municipality counts.
data.access: Rapid transit access — straight-line distance from each cell center to the nearest active tram, rail or player metro stop.
data.concepts: Past concepts — schematic drafts shipped with this region.
data.demand: The selected grid contains {{residents}} residents. We group them into {{zones}} municipality-based anchors. Origins use residential population; destinations use a separate estimate based on local density and proximity to the municipal population center. This is not an observed work, school or retail zoning dataset. At {{rate}} assumed cross-zone trip opportunities per resident per day, this produces {{trips}} modeled opportunities.
data.method: Paths use stop sequences, walking transfers, the selected period's interval and scheduled run times. A route's average initial wait is half its interval. The Peak, Midday and Saturday control describes that period; the clock minute does not change the model. Passenger count is a simulated transit share, never an observed count.
data.satisfaction: Satisfaction is an index based on modeled journey time, which already includes waiting and transfer penalties. The local results are grouped by trip origin. Cost is route-kilometers × departures × assumed cost per kilometer (bus zł12, tram zł20, rail zł38, metro zł55). Peak uses Wednesday trip counts. Another period uses that period's stored trip count, or Wednesday trips scaled by the peak interval divided by the period interval when no count was stored. These values support relative experiments, not official forecasts.
data.shapes: Each GTFS route uses one representative shape per direction; branches and short turns are simplified. Ordinary player lines run both ways; rings run in the drawn order and include their closing segment. New lines, PKM patterns and edited stops use direct segments. Play moves illustrative vehicles, not real-time positions.
